tools.name: fuse_tiers
tools.description:
What Fuse can generate right now, read live from the account's pricing: each tier's three axes (mode, priority, quality), its token price, the resolutions it offers with the per-second rate for each, its aspect ratios, and whether it accepts a last frame. Nothing in this package hardcodes these — call this before quoting or creating a project.

audio says what the clip's own soundtrack will be, which pricing cannot carry because audio is free wherever a tier has it and pricing carries prices. audio.sound is how firmly it is known: always (Fuse asks for it), observed (Fuse asks for nothing, the provider's default has so far returned sound) or unknown (nothing asked, nothing measured).

None of that is the voice-over. A video model invents speech that reads nobody's script and can be a different person in every scene, so the narration always comes from fuse_narration or the customer's own file, on every tier. Tell them while the tier is being chosen: the voice is a second budget on a second account whatever they pick, and a tier that arrives with sound adds a track to mute rather than one to save. It is a claim about a model, not a measurement: fuse_manifest measures the clips themselves, and where the two disagree the manifest is right.

tools.name: fuse_upload
tools.description:
Uploads image files from this machine to the customer's own Fuse account and returns a public URL for each. Costs no tokens.

This is what makes image-to-video usable. An i2v tier reads its start frame over HTTP — the API fetches the URL itself — so a photo sitting on the customer's disk cannot be sent to it. Upload it here first, then pass the url straight into fuse_scenes as imageUrls (or lastImageUrl).

The files land in the account's own asset library, where the customer can see them on the web, and the URL is a plain public storage link with no key in it — so do not upload anything they would not put on a public URL. Ask before uploading a file they did not point at.

files.description: Paths to image files on this machine, absolute or relative to the working directory. How many an i2v tier accepts is the tier's own rule, not this limit.

groupId.description: Files uploaded together land in one folder under this name. Pass the project's job id to keep an ad's images together; a new one is made when it is left out.

tools.name: fuse_quote
tools.description: Token cost of a set of scenes on one tier, without creating or charging anything. The total is a floor: the ledger charges on the clip the provider returns, which can run slightly longer than the duration asked for. Use it to agree a budget with the user, then pass that budget as fuse_scenes' maxTokens.

tier.description: A tier id from fuse_tiers, e.g. t2v-low-standard.

resolution.description: A resolution name offered by that tier, as fuse_tiers lists it, e.g. 480p.

seconds.description: Clip length in seconds. The valid range belongs to the tier; the API states it.

scenes.description: The scenes to price. Prompts are not needed for a quote.

tools.name: fuse_project_new
tools.description:
Creates a video project on this machine: HyperFrames' own scaffold (its config, its skills, its CLAUDE.md), a place for the clips, and Noto Sans Thai as local files so Thai captions render instead of turning into tofu boxes. The tier, resolution and aspect are fixed here for the whole job, which is why fuse_scenes does not take them again. It does NOT report a canvas size: the real pixel box differs between providers serving the same nominal resolution, so it is measured from the clips by fuse_manifest once they exist.

The first call on a machine that has never rendered fetches HyperFrames and a browser, which can take longer than the client allows one tool call. That is harmless and the work is kept: call it again with the same arguments and it carries on from the scaffold it left. It will refuse to re-bind an existing project to a different tier.

dir.description: The project directory, absolute or relative to where this server was started.

tier.description: A tier id from fuse_tiers, e.g. t2v-low-standard.

resolution.description: A resolution name offered by that tier, as fuse_tiers lists it, e.g. 480p.

aspect.description: An aspect ratio the tier offers, as fuse_tiers lists it, e.g. 16:9.

fonts.description: Fetch Noto Sans Thai into the project. Turn off only for a Latin-only ad.

tools.name: fuse_scenes
tools.description:
Generates every named scene and downloads the clips into the project. This is the only tool that spends tokens, and maxTokens is the ceiling for the whole project, including what it has already spent: if the scenes would go over it, nothing is submitted and nothing is charged.

It blocks for up to waitMs (45 s by default, because a client commonly cuts a tool call off at 60 s) and then reports what is done. Call it again with the same arguments to keep waiting — a scene that was already paid for is never submitted twice, so re-calling costs nothing and resumes after a crash, a new session or a top-up. Renaming a scene's slug does not re-charge it either; editing its prompt or duration does, because that is a different clip.

A stopped field says why it gave up early (insufficient_tokens, over_budget, rejected_by_api, provider_failed) and detail carries the server's own words — read them, they hold the real rule, such as the duration range for the tier.

dir.description: The project directory, absolute or relative to where this server was started.

maxTokens.description: Token ceiling for this project in total, already-spent included. Required: agree it with the user from fuse_quote.

seconds.description: Clip length in seconds. The valid range belongs to the tier; the API states it.

imageUrls.description: Reference images for an image-to-video tier, as public URLs the API can fetch. How many are allowed is the tier's rule.

lastImageUrl.description: The frame to end on, where the tier supports one.

waitMs.description: How long to wait before reporting partial progress. Keep it under the client's own tool-call timeout, which is 60 s unless the client raises it: a longer block does not report progress, it fails. Calling again waits on, for free.

tools.name: fuse_manifest
tools.description:
Reads every downloaded clip with ffprobe and writes assets/scenes/manifest.json: the canvas to compose on, each clip's real duration, the frame rate the clips carry and whether they came back with sound. All of it has to be measured. The same nominal 480p 16:9 came back as 864x480 from one provider and 832x480 from another, and a 5 second ask came back as 5.167 s — so use this canvas for the composition's data-width/data-height, its CSS box and its viewport, and these durations for the timing. A guessed canvas upscales the footage and multiplies render time.

fps goes on the root as data-fps: HyperFrames renders at 30 unless told otherwise, so 24 fps footage left alone is delivered with a duplicate of every fifth frame. When fps is absent nothing reported a rate — say so rather than picking one.

hasAudio is what the provider returned, not what the tier promises, and it is the measurement that settles any disagreement with fuse_tiers. When it is true the clip carries a soundtrack nobody wrote: keep it on the <video> (data-has-audio, no muted) only where it works as atmosphere under the piece. Where the scene has narration, or the model is audibly speaking, mute it — model speech reads nobody's script and changes voice between scenes.

dir.description: The project directory, absolute or relative to where this server was started.

tools.name: fuse_voices
tools.description:
The voices this ElevenLabs account can speak with, the text-to-speech models it may use and the languages each one covers, and how many characters are left this period. Costs nothing.

Voiceover runs on the customer's own ElevenLabs account, never on Fuse: these characters are billed by ElevenLabs and no Fuse token is involved. Show the list and let the user pick — a voice is the ad's presenter, so it is their choice to make, not one to default. Pass the id they choose to fuse_narration.

Check that the model you intend to use lists the script's language: a model that does not speak Thai will mispronounce a Thai script and charge for it all the same.

search.description: Narrow the list by name, description, label or category. Useful on an account with more voices than one page holds.

tools.name: fuse_narration
tools.description:
Writes one mp3 per line into assets/audio/ in the voice the user chose, and reports each file's measured duration so the picture can be timed to the voice.

This spends the customer's ElevenLabs character allowance, not Fuse tokens. Call it first with dryRun true: that prices every line, spends nothing and touches nothing, and the figure it reports is the one to agree with the user. maxCharacters is then the ceiling for the real call — if the lines would go over it, nothing is spoken and nothing is charged.

Safe to call again. A line whose exact words were already spoken in the same voice is reused from disk for free, so a call cut off by a timeout carries on instead of paying for the script twice. Renaming a scene is free; editing a word is new audio, because it is. Two scenes that say the same thing share one file.

A stopped field says why it gave up early (over_budget, quota_exhausted, rejected_by_api, provider_failed) and detail carries ElevenLabs' own words.

dir.description: The project directory, absolute or relative to where this server was started.

voiceId.description: A voice id from fuse_voices — the one the user picked, not a default.

modelId.description: A model id from fuse_voices. Defaults to eleven_multilingual_v2, which speaks Thai.

maxCharacters.description: Character ceiling for this call. Required: get the figure from a dryRun call and agree it with the user, the same way maxTokens is agreed for the clips.

dryRun.description: Price the script and speak none of it. Nothing is charged or written.

text.description: Exactly what is said in this scene. Punctuation shapes the delivery.
